correctness.rationale: At a stationary time, the independent backward Poisson intervals have rate r. Conditional on their lengths, the reset sum is centered Gaussian with covariance (2D/r) T_q I_d, where q=b² and T_q=Σ_{j≥0} q^j E_j with iid unit-rate exponentials. This proves the sign invariance and gives P_d=(r/(4πD))^(d/2) E[T_q^(−d/2)]. The stationary construction converges in L²; shared-noise coupling shrinks an arbitrary initial displacement by a^{N_t} almost surely, proving uniqueness. The radial Fourier transform Φ_b(u)=Π_{j≥0}(1+b^{2j}u²)^(−1) is bounded at large u by any fixed finite leading product, giving integrability against every polynomial and hence a bounded smooth density. The identity Φ_b(bu)−Φ_b(u)=u²Φ_b(u) gives I_{d+2}=(b^(−d)−1)I_d and C_{d+2}/C_d=1/(2πd). For d=2, integrate [Φ_b(bu)−Φ_b(u)]/u; Tonelli with the decreasing function's derivative integrates over v≤u≤v/b, giving I_2=log(1/b). For the odd anchor the tail of the log product is bounded by u²b²/(1−b²), and Φ_b(u)≤1/(1+u²), so I_1→π/2 by dominated convergence. Iteration gives the exponents n(n−1) and n² and the stated constants, including the finite d=1 limit. At b=0 the conditional variance uses only E_0, whose inverse d/2 moment diverges for d≥2. All contraction limits keep d,D,r fixed. evidence: Set H(p)=E[(I^(q))^(−p)]. In Eq. (1.7) put s=−p to obtain H(p)=Γ(1−p)(q^{1−p};q)_∞/(q;q)_∞. The single vanishing factor at p=1 cancels the gamma pole, giving H(1)=log(1/q); at p=1/2 the q-product tends to one as q↓0, so H(1/2)→√π.

Dividing adjacent orders in the same formula gives H(p+1)/H(p)=(q^{−p}−1)/p, by the gamma and product cancellation identities. Inserting p=d/2 and q=b² gives the exact dimension ladder and P_2=(r/(2πD)) log(1/b). The finite products yield the even exponent Σ_{j=1}^{n−1}2j and the odd exponent Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}(2j+1), with the stated prefactors.

originality.rationale: The full contact law, including the claimed planar anchor, dimension shift and both parity asymptotics, is a direct specialization of a published stronger Mellin transform, not merely similar to a one- or three-dimensional resetting result. The stationary contact is the negative moment at s=−d/2 of the very same weighted-exponential variable in Bertoin–Biane–Yor (2004), Eq. (1.3) and Theorem 1.1(i), Eq. (1.7). The frozen proof's frequency integral is equivalently that same negative moment times Γ(d/2)/2. This is positive prior-coverage evidence, not a priority inference from failed access or a title match.
residual_risks: The cited Kolb–Wübker primary text was not retrieved; it could refine special-case credit, but is not needed for demonstrated coverage.
No claim is made about who first wrote the Brownian contact law in this terminology, or about the earliest historical q-integral antecedent. The demonstrated stronger 2004 moment result suffices.

value.rationale: The contact density is a naturally motivated diagnostic, and the direct elementary derivation is readable. But the frozen contribution is an exact contact law obtained mechanically from a stronger known invariant of the identical effective-time distribution. The planar anchor, ladder and parity hierarchy are all covered, including fixed-rate prefactors after rescaling; the package supplies no additional nonmechanical conclusion about the resetting process. Re-expressing the Mellin identity or reproducing its values by quadrature does not establish an independent scientific contribution.
